brief: Last Thursday investors bought a record 55.8 million puts (3.4x the 10-year average), the biggest hedging day ever, one week after the midterms hit the AI trade; by Monday they were dumping protection at a near-record pace. Goldman's vol desk reads this as light positioning (net leverage at a 5-year low, 43.3%), a jittery Panic Index (6.5/10) and a vol-of-vol spike (VVIX realized vol to 208) that together make the hedges themselves the most volatile asset. The desk still likes owning S&P downside skew, since dealers are structurally short vol on the way down and long on the way up. It also pitched selling volatility on Nvidia via a costless call spread collar (ref $166.50, 10% cushion) to add exposure cheaply. The stock closed Wednesday at $173.73, but a same-day NYT/WSJ report that the board may remove Huang sent it down 8.6% after hours to $158.78, burning 47% of the cushion in hours. Separately, Goldman flags small-cap and biopharma volatility as cheap, buying IWM calls, even though hot CPI and a forecast third 2027 rate hike cut against rate-sensitive small caps.
